title: Openness of the unrestricted fibre Cohen-Macaulay locus
statement: Let f:X→T be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The set of y∈X for which the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] of the local ring of the fibre X_{f(y)} at y [def-pc-scheme-fibre; def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] equals its ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] is open in X.

source.place: Tag 045U (1), (2), its affine openness input Tag 00RI, and Tag 00N8

proof.text: Prove preservation of self-module depth under local ring isomorphisms directly from the definition: the maximal ideal maps to the maximal ideal, and mapping a regular sequence along the isomorphism preserves regularity and length. Apply both directions and antisymmetry to the suprema defining depth. Krull dimension is invariant under ring isomorphisms by Mathlib.

For a source open immersion i:U to X, form the pullback map from the fibre of i followed by f to the corresponding fibre of f. It is an open immersion by MorphismProperty.pullbackMap. Its composite with the original fibre inclusion is the source fibre inclusion followed by i, so it sends asFiber x to asFiber (i x), by injectivity of the original fibre inclusion. Its stalk map is an isomorphism. Apply the first step to obtain equivalence of the two depth-equals-dimension conditions. This is fibre_locus_source_iff in Lean.

For a base open immersion i:V to T, pull f back along i. Mathlib isPullback_fiberToSpecResidueField_of_isPullback gives the pullback square on scheme fibres. The residue-field map of an open immersion is an isomorphism, so its base change identifies the two fibres. Transport the base point by the pullback commutativity equation, check the image of asFiber using the fibre inclusions, and apply the induced stalk isomorphism and the first step. This is fibre_locus_base_iff in Lean.

When the base is affine, cover the source by its Mathlib affineCover. The composites of the cover maps with f are flat and locally of finite presentation, with affine source and target. Apply the affine fibre-locus theorem to each composite and the source comparison from the second step. Each preimage of the desired locus is open. The locus equals the union of the images of these preimages because the cover is jointly surjective. Each image is open because the cover map is an open immersion.

For arbitrary base, pull back its affineCover along f. Each pullback morphism to the affine cover member is flat and locally of finite presentation by stability under base change, so the previous step applies. The base comparison from the third step identifies its locus with the preimage of the original locus under the source cover map. Again the locus is the union of open images of open preimages under this jointly surjective open cover. This argument also covers the empty source or base: the union is empty.

proof_origin.place: Tag 045U (1), (2): affine-cover reduction. The source and base fibre comparisons, ring-isomorphism invariance of depth, and open-cover gluing are proved directly from Mathlib in Lean; Tag 00RI remains the separate affine input.

lean.statement:
theorem isOpen_fibre_depth_eq_ringKrullDim
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    IsOpen {y : X |
      (IsLocalRing.depth (R := (f.fiber (f y)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber y))
        ((f.fiber (f y)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber y)) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
          ringKrullDim ((f.fiber (f y)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber y))}
